newsitem.title: USA: U.S. ACCESS crude prices trade in narrow range.
newsitem.headline: U.S. ACCESS crude prices trade in narrow range.

text.p: U.S. ACCESS energy prices traded in a narrow range after a day of nervous activity, with little news and values forecast to fall with heating oil Friday.
"We'll try to take this market off a little bit," one trader said, noting that heating oil, which rose 0.73 cent to end 72.29 cents a gallon, had underperformed the past two weeks.
Heating oil edged up 0.11 cent to 72.40 cents a gallon in light after-hours trade. The front-month traded 79 lots while total volume hit 105.
Daytime prices fluctuated widely for a second-straight day as data from the Energy Information Administration (EIA) showed draws larger than reported earlier by API.
The market also turned jittery ahead of Friday's meeting between energy officials and oil companies to discuss ways to temper the effects of heating oil shortages this winter.
November crude oil traded $25.44 a barrel, two cents over the settle, with bids at $25.41. Approximately 266 lots traded in the front month, with 781 traded total.
Front-month gasoline gained 0.07 cent to 66.60 cents a gallon on ACCESS, with a paltry eight contracts traded -- all in November.
